answer: A Tri-Vertex Pigment Bond stops Sybil swarms by tying each identity to three verifiers forming one vertex of trust. First, the agent locks 250 POA and a 0.02 BNB fee for 90 days. Second, each verifier checks a live behavioral signal - history, latency, stake age - and stamps the identity with a unique pigment marker uncopyable without redoing all three checks. Third, a duplicate marker slashes the 250 POA and bans the agent 180 days. Faking 1,000 identities costs 250,000 POA, 20 BNB, and 3,000 checks. Like dye bonding to one cloth, the pigment marks one real agent, not a thousand copies.
